events.description: A bright, star-like flash with radiating light beams and a purple core appears, consistent with a sudden energy release or explosion in space or atmospheric context.
A second distinct explosive event: a bright blue-white flash with radial beams and a surrounding luminous ring (possibly shockwave or plasma ring), occurring independently of the first.
A third intense explosion: a central brilliant white-blue starburst with multiple sharp light rays and surrounding debris trails; appears to be the culmination of prior activity.

A bright, star-like energy burst with multiple radial beams appears and intensifies, consistent with a high-energy explosion or impact event; visible as a purple-white flash at f0, expanding into a multi-rayed burst by f1 and f6.

A secondary, larger-scale explosive effect manifests as a circular shockwave/ring expanding outward from the initial burst site, interacting with terrain; visible as a glowing ring at f5, evolving into a structured expanding disc by f14–f15.

A large, bright white explosion erupts on the left side of the landscape, rapidly expanding and producing a mushroom-like cloud; this is visually distinct from ambient light or aurora and matches the definition of a sudden blast.

A massive, luminous spherical energy burst forms overhead, radiating intense beams downward and outward; it evolves from the earlier explosion and culminates in a structured, high-energy detonation with visible shockwave-like structures and particle trails—consistent with a large-scale explosion event.
